title: Introduce invocation telemetry lighthouse panels and quiet-window adaptive alerting
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers and SREs need a compact, actionable view that surfaces per-route and per-tenant cost+latency hotspots together with stable log samples for triage. Existing dashboards show separate cost and latency curves but lack a single-pane 'lighthouse' view that highlights offending routes, the dominant token-phase causing cost, and a representative (stable) log sample to attach to incidents. This PR adds: 1) A Lighthouse dashboard JSON that mixes per-route heatmap, phased token-cost bars, and a ranked 'hotpath' table for top N routes; 2) Quiet-window adaptive alerting: an alert tuning algorithm that detects low-noise windows and reduces alert sensitivity dynamically to suppress churn from long-tail token bursts; 3) A log-sample stabilizer that picks deterministic representative log snippets for repeated anomalies to improve RCA quality.

Design summary:
- Lighthouse panels: a composite dashboard (redwood/observability/dashboards/lighthouse.json) which contains:
  * Invocation heatmap: per-route x-axis, percentile y-axis, color by weighted cost delta.
  * Token-phase stacked bars: CPU vs GPU token phases per-route with normalized cost units.
  * Representative sample column: pointer to a stable log sample key (see stabilizer below).
- Quiet-window adaptive alerting: implemented as a controller (telemetry/alerting/quiet_window_controller.go) that consumes a short rolling window of per-route noise metrics (entropy of token phase mix, burst rate) and adjusts alert thresholds per-route with a hysteresis model to avoid flip-flops. Configurable knobs: MinQuietWindowSeconds, SensitivityScale, MaxSuppressionPct.
- Log-sample stabilizer: telemetry/logs/sample_stabilizer.go keeps a small reservoir keyed by invocation fingerprint (hash of prompt shape + route + truncated prompt id) and prefers samples seen multiple times in the last 24h. This reduces noise in alert payloads and ensures consistent samples are attached to automated ticket summaries.

Implementation notes and changed files:
- redwood/observability/dashboards/lighthouse.json: new dashboard definition. Snippet: {"panels": [{"type": "heatmap", "title": "Invocation heatmap (cost-weighted)"}, {"type": "table", "title": "Top hotpaths"}]}
- telemetry/alerting/quiet_window_controller.go: new controller with tests and a lightweight state store. Key function: EvaluateQuietWindow(routeStats) -> adjustmentFactor
- telemetry/logs/sample_stabilizer.go: new stabilizer with reservoir sampling + TTL eviction
- telemetry/collector/consumer.go: minor changes to emit phase-entropy metric and stable_sample_key tag
- observability/agents/README.md: documentation on how to enable the lighthouse dashboard and safe rollout notes

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: added stabilizer and quiet window controller unit tests (stable across synthetic random seeds).
- Integration tests: dashboard rendering smoke test added to observability CI job to validate JSON schema and panel queries.
- Load validation: synthetic replay of 10k invocations across 50 routes to validate controller state growth under peak.

CI history: initial run failed one flaky end-to-end dashboard-render test (timeout under heavy CI load); rerun passed.

Performance: quiet-window controller is deliberately O(R) with small constant overhead (R = number of routes active in window). Under synthetic load it consumed <2% CPU on a medium-sized telemetry fleet worker.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable lighthouse read-only dashboard for internal SRE tenants and enable stabilizer sampling only for routes prefixed with /internal/
- Stage 2: enable quiet-window controller in monitor-only mode (no threshold changes) for one week and record suggested adjustments
- Stage 3: enable adaptive suppression at 10% max suppression and monitor alert churn metrics; escalate to 25% if alert noise drops without missing incidents
- Full rollout after 2 weeks of canary if no regressions

Checklist:
- [x] Dashboard JSON validated with schema validator
- [x] Unit/integration tests added
- [x] Performance smoke test executed
- [x] Documentation updated - observability/agents/README.md
- [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-3891, ENG-4012)

Backwards compatibility: No breaking changes to public telemetry APIs; stabilizer exposes a new optional tag stable_sample_key but does not change schemas.

Request for reviewers: Please focus review on quiet_window_controller.go correctness (concurrency and state eviction), dashboard panel queries for cost-weight normalization, and the log-sample key collision risk model.

TL;DR: Adds a composite 'Lighthouse' observability dashboard, an adaptive alert-suppression controller (quiet-window), and a log-sample stabilizer to attach consistent triage artifacts to alerts.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: General approach LGTM. Two concerns: (1) eviction correctness under clock skew; please add monotonic-timestamp based eviction. (2) Need guardrails around max memory per-controller.
Maya Chen: Reply: switched to monotonic epoch counters for eviction and added a soft memory cap with metric emittance when exceeded (telemetry.alert.quiet_window.mem_exhausted).
Lucia Moreno: The dashboard queries look heavy for high-card routes. Can we add a bounded cardinality clause?
Maya Chen: Reply: added query filters to the dashboard to limit initial lookup to top 250 routes by P50 cost; controller exposes a "route_cardinality_cap" config for operators.
release_notes: Introduce Lighthouse observability dashboard (cost+latency heatmap + representative samples). Add quiet-window adaptive alerting to reduce alert churn during low-noise periods. Add log-sample stabilizer for consistent incident attachments. Configurable and staged rollout.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps adaptive suppression conservative by default. If we see false negatives we can adjust SensitivityScale and MaxSuppressionPct via feature flags.
